comparator.name: Bachelor Systems Engineering, Policy Analysis and Management
comparator.sourceNotes: The official programme page describes a three-year, four-quarter structure with three modules per quarter, a 30-EC minor in the first half of Year 3, electives and a Bachelor Final Project. The official 2026–27 module map specifies the compulsory analysis, governance, quantitative-methods, programming/modelling and skills strands, plus one of three technology domains: Energy & Industry, Data & Digitalisation, or Transport & Logistics. The 180-EC component accounting groups the modules exactly as displayed by study year and strand; it does not invent a specific minor.
components: One of Energy & Industry, Data & Digitalisation, or Transport & Logistics.
Simulation, research and multivariate data analysis
Continuation of the selected technology domain.
Genuine open minor space; no specific TU Delft minor is invented.
Governance specialisation and governance of socio-technical systems
Advanced course in the selected technology domain.
Compulsory independent final project in Technical Public Administration.

core: Analysis and governance of complex socio-technical systems
Organisations, markets, institutions, law, ethics and stakeholder conflict
Mathematical modelling, statistics, programming, simulation and decision analysis
adjacent: Energy and industry systems, infrastructure and transition governance
Data, digitalisation and responsible technology governance
Transport, logistics and resilient infrastructure governance
questions: How can policy and governance reconcile actors with conflicting public and private interests?
How can models, data and decision methods compare policy options under uncertainty?
How should technological infrastructure and innovation be governed responsibly?

alternatives.label: Energy, infrastructure & transition governance
alternatives.labelReason: This pathway most closely combines systems analysis, quantitative decision methods, organisational governance and policy with a sustained energy-transition and infrastructure emphasis.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to Technical Public Administration: a socio-technical systems programme combining modelling, data, organisations, ethics, public decisions and energy-transition governance.
progression: Programming, data, business, statistics and sustainability foundations precede system modelling, research methods, governance, organisations, sustainability analysis, applied research and advanced energy-system design. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Data, digitalisation & public decisions
alternatives.labelReason: This pathway gives greater weight to mathematical modelling, algorithms, machine learning, neural networks, digital transformation and the governance implications of AI.
alternatives.concept: A data-and-digitalisation direction connecting policy and organisational analysis with mathematical modelling, algorithms, machine learning, optimisation and responsible digital transformation.
progression: Programming, data, business and statistics foundations precede linear algebra, numerical methods, digital transformation, algorithms, organisational leadership, optimisation and neural networks. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: Relative to the closest programme, this route replaces four sustainability and energy courses with linear algebra, numerical methods, algorithms and neural networks. The programmes differ by four courses and 30 EC in each direction.

alternatives.label: Transport, logistics & infrastructure governance
alternatives.labelReason: This pathway centres resilient infrastructure, water and land-use systems, international business governance and sustainability governance as UCR’s closest feasible transport-and-logistics policy direction.
alternatives.concept: A transport-and-infrastructure direction linking quantitative decisions and organisational governance to mobility, logistics, resilient infrastructure, international governance and sustainability policy.
progression: Programming, data, business, statistics and sustainability foundations precede resilient-infrastructure design, water management, digital transformation, international business governance, organisational leadership and advanced sustainability governance. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: Relative to each earlier programme, this route replaces four domain courses with a distinct set in nature-based infrastructure, water governance, international business governance and sustainability governance. Every pair differs by four courses and 30 EC in each direction.

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
trace: Introduction to Programming develops Python-based computational problem solving for socio-technical models and policy data.
Introduction to Data Science develops data cleaning, visualisation and analysis for evidence-based public decisions.
Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations introduces organisations, markets, value creation and stakeholder-oriented decisions.
Research Methods & Statistics develops empirical research design and statistical reasoning under uncertainty.
Database Management Systems develops the data-infrastructure foundations of digital socio-technical systems.
AI Ethics examines fairness, responsibility and governance questions created by intelligent technologies.
Mathematical Methods supplies calculus, linear algebra and differential-equation tools for system modelling.
Logic & Discrete Mathematics develops formal reasoning for computational systems and decisions.
Statistics & Experimental Methods develops multivariate analysis and evidence evaluation for complex human systems.
Sustainability Essentials I introduces linked technical, environmental and societal systems.
Strategy & Digital Transformation examines organisational strategy and responsible change under technological disruption.
Qualitative Research Methodology supports actor, stakeholder and institutional analysis.
Ethics provides normative tools for weighing competing public and private interests.
Psychology of Organizations & Leadership analyses organisational behaviour, coordination and leadership.
Persuasive Communication develops evidence-based argumentation for stakeholders and public decisions.
European Union Politics examines institutions, multi-level governance and policy-making.
Business & Economy in the Age of AI examines organisational, economic, governance and regulatory consequences of AI.
Market Research applies quantitative and qualitative evidence to stakeholder and decision problems.
Optimization Methods in AI develops formal optimisation for decisions in complex systems.
Climate Change establishes the technical and governance context of the energy transition.
Sustainability Essentials II develops integrated systems analysis for technology, environment and society.
Research in a Sustainable Delta provides applied interdisciplinary research with an external partner.
Renewable System Design integrates technical and economic assessment of energy systems in an external-company project.
Linear Algebra supplies matrix methods for system models, data analysis and optimisation.
Computational & Numerical Methods develops numerical modelling for complex systems.
Algorithms & Data Structures develops efficient computational methods for complex data and systems.
Neural Networks & Deep Learning develops advanced modelling of complex data.
Building with Nature examines resilient infrastructure, land reclamation and flood protection.
Living with Water examines infrastructure, land use, water governance and competing interests.
International Business & Governance examines institutional and political forces shaping cross-border infrastructure and organisations.
Governance of Sustainability examines actors, institutions, interests and public policy for complex transitions.
blocks: Systems analysis, modelling and quantitative decisions
Introduction to Programming directly addresses the programming foundation, with different scope and credits.
AI Ethics addresses the ethics-and-safety function for digital technologies, with narrower technical scope.
Mathematical Methods addresses calculus, linear algebra and differential-equation foundations, with different breadth and credits.
Statistics & Experimental Methods addresses multivariate data analysis and research methods, without reproducing the full TU Delft simulation sequence.
Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations addresses organisations, markets and economics, but not the full TU Delft law-and-governance sequence.
Strategy & Digital Transformation addresses organisational and institutional responses to technological change, with different infrastructure depth.
Psychology of Organizations & Leadership contributes advanced organisational analysis, but UCR does not reproduce the dedicated governance specialisation.
Sustainability Essentials I contributes integrated systems thinking, while TU Delft provides a dedicated socio-technical analysis sequence.
Climate Change supports the Energy & Industry domain through energy-transition and climate-governance analysis.
Sustainability Essentials II continues integrated systems analysis relevant to the energy domain, with different technical depth.
Renewable System Design provides advanced technical-economic energy-system work aligned with the Energy & Industry domain.
Research Methods & Statistics supports independent empirical work but does not reproduce the compulsory 15-EC TU Delft bachelor final project.
The genuine 30-EC minor space is preserved without inventing a specific TU Delft minor.

selection.assessment: The programme-wide systems, governance and quantitative core supports a closest Energy & Industry pathway. The official Data & Digitalisation and Transport & Logistics domains each support a further coherent UCR curriculum with material course consequences. All three pass feasibility and the pairwise 30-EC distinctness floor, so production stops at the permitted maximum.

notes.text: TU Delft integrates engineering-style socio-technical systems analysis, governance, economics, law, mathematics, statistics, programming, simulation, a selected technology domain and a compulsory 15-EC final project. UCR can build substantial interdisciplinary pathways across data science, business, politics, ethics and sustainability, but distributes them across clusters and does not reproduce the same prescribed engineering-and-policy sequence.

The TU Delft degree provides a deeper continuous sequence in system modelling, multi-actor analysis, infrastructure economics, simulation and domain-specific technology than any fixed UCR pathway. The UCR alternatives are academically coherent comparisons, not claims of professional or curricular equivalence.
